title: Article 32 — Remedies for enforcement of rights conferred by Part III

content.overview: Article 32 guarantees the right to move the Supreme Court by appropriate proceedings for the enforcement of the rights conferred by Part III. It is itself a Fundamental Right. The Supreme Court may issue directions, orders or writs including habeas corpus, mandamus, prohibition, quo warranto and certiorari.

sections.heading: Fundamental right to constitutional remedy
sections.body: Article 32 is not merely procedural; the right to move the Supreme Court for Part III enforcement is itself guaranteed.

sections.heading: Writs
sections.body: The five classic writs are available as appropriate. Choice of writ follows the nature of the wrong (detention, public duty, excess of jurisdiction, usurpation of office, etc.).

sections.heading: Article 32 vs Article 226
sections.body: Article 226 is the High Court’s power to issue writs for Fundamental Rights and for any other purpose. It is wider in remedial subject-matter but is not itself a Fundamental Right. Territorial limits under Article 226(2) apply. Alternative remedy is a rule of discretion, not want of jurisdiction, with recognised exceptions.

sections.heading: Track B
sections.body: Frame the Part III right, the State action, and the appropriate writ. Consider whether the High Court under Article 226 is the more suitable forum. See also the PIL subject set for standing practice.
